crossApp.name: reference-palette-distance
crossApp.detail: mean ΔE2000 from the reference's top colors to the template palette (reported, not gated)

notes: Overall: the base language transfers well. Warm paper, ink-only actions, chips that invert to ink, segmented control with a paper segment, 2px ink tab underline, hairline cards, mono numbers right-aligned, deep status badges with dot and word. Dark 'night paper' surfaces, text and inverted paper buttons are warm and well judged. The signature studio details are where it breaks.

CONFIRMED, bloom clipped into a rectangle: blog home, blog about, commerce home and dashboard overview (desktop, light and dark) all show a straight vertical right edge and a straight horizontal bottom edge. Blog clips at the 1360 container edge (x=1360), commerce at x=1400, dashboard at the viewport edge, and all clip at the bottom of the header (y around 270-330). The cause is the spec recipe itself, not agent invention: blog base.css .has-bloom follows the recipe literally ('position: relative; overflow: hidden' on the header section) with a 700x560 SVG at top:-120px, but the header is only around 250px tall and sits inside the container. 560-120 = 440px of bloom gets cut at about 250px. Where the reference bleeds organically off the viewport, the template ships a gray-lavender swatch in a box.

CONFIRMED, one-word titles set entirely in serif italic: dashboard 'Overview' and all four settings titles ('Profile', 'Notifications', 'Security', 'Billing'). Each reads as a font switch rather than an accent, which loses the tight-grotesk voice in the one place it should be strongest. Rule 6 ('one serif italic word per page title') literally permits this, so it is a spec gap. The settings spec also says the serif word is optional, and the agent still applied it to every screen. Serif use differs across apps: blog puts it on every title; commerce only on the collection header, with no serif on product or cart; dashboard only on Overview; settings on every page.

Dark-mode bloom: on blog, commerce and dashboard dark the bloom renders as a muddy dark-slate smudge with a darker rim, close to the page color. It reads as a stain, not a wash, and it is still clipped to a rectangle. The analysis asked for 'no grain darkening' in dark, but the single shared mn-wash filter (rim plus grain) is used in both themes.

Mobile bloom overlaps secondary text: blog home ('Essays on building software...'), commerce home ('Durable bags, clothing and kitchen goods') and dashboard overview ('across all teams for October 2026') at 390px. This violates 'Only an h1 or display heading may overlap the bloom', and the spec's own mobile geometry (360x288, top -60, right -140) makes the overlap close to unavoidable on a 390 viewport. The dashboard and blog mobile blooms also show a straight bottom clip.

Studio-detail limits are respected: at most 1 bloom per screen, the blog featured post is the only taped and pinned item (2 strips), there are no details in tables, forms, cart, product, settings or dialogs, and the swash appears once per app family. No pencil notes appear in any app, so a defining reference mark is absent everywhere. The spec makes notes optional and no base app has an onboarding moment.

Text field collapse: blog home 'Search posts' (desktop and mobile, both themes) and dashboard mobile 'Filter projects' render as a roughly 20px-tall pill instead of size.control 40px with radius.control 9. The spec already defines the height, so this is an agent mistake. The input's height comes from line-height inside a flex row with align-items:center. It also throws off the chip row: chips sit lower than the input.

Mobile navigation: dashboard at 390px keeps every sidebar link in a horizontal top row that runs off-screen ('Set...' cut off) with no menu button. The agent report says it skipped the menu sheet. Settings mobile turns the sidebar into a pill-tab row (current item on a well) that fits only by luck.

Mobile overflow: settings security mobile (both themes) captures at 1010px wide for a 390px viewport. The sessions table pushes the document to about 505 css px, the 'Last active' column is cut and the Revoke buttons are unreachable without page-level horizontal scroll. Dashboard mobile tables squeeze project names to 3-4 lines, and 'Due date' is pushed out of the frame with no scroll affordance.

Commerce mobile product page does build the sticky action bar (52px ink button, radius.callout, bar surface), which is good. In the full-page capture the fixed bar covers the Quantity label and stepper. That is largely a capture artifact, but the page has no bottom padding equal to the bar height, so the last content can sit under the bar in real use too.

Media placeholders are inconsistent and off-spec: blog articles use a large filled mountain-and-sun glyph in grey on the tray (clip-art, which the Never list forbids as filled illustration), while commerce uses a 16px outline image icon on a flat tray with no hatch. Neither uses the specified hatch.

Switch off-state is nearly invisible: settings notifications off tracks ('Weekly summary', 'Comments', 'Reminders') are color.surface.subtle with a color.border.strong edge on white. That is about 1.4:1 in light and close to invisible on #1d1c18 in dark, below the 3:1 non-text contrast a control boundary needs. The spec defines this exact recipe, so it is a spec gap.

Hierarchy: commerce product pages set the product name at page-h1 56px ('Canvas Field Tote', 'Merino Crew Sweater' wraps to two lines in a narrow column), which dwarfs the price and Add to cart. Dashboard Projects stacks h1 'Projects' directly over h2 'All projects'. The project detail page floats the 'Active' badge alone at the far right edge, disconnected from the title.

Spacing: the dashboard 'Deployment throughput' card stretches to match 'Recent activity' and leaves about 150px of dead space under the chart. The blog featured card is a fixed 880px (agent's own choice), which leaves an empty right column on a 1360 container. The blog footer note at the right does not align with the newsletter block. Otherwise card padding, block gaps of 56-64 and hairline rows are consistent across all four apps.

Mono rule applied unevenly: dashboard tables and billing amounts are mono, but billing invoice dates, the dashboard project-detail values ($240,000, Dec 15, 2026) and the commerce product spec rows are not. Commerce 'Details' rows have no mono key column, so they are not the specified spec-row pattern.

Component states visible in the captures: selected chip, segmented control, tab, sidebar current, radio-card selection (2px ink ring), current-plan ring, switch on/off, disabled quantity minus button, sort chevron, cart empty state (pinned, no details, correct for cart). Focus, hover, error, loading and toast states are not captured anywhere, so the gates cannot vouch for them. Both agent reports state that nothing was built or viewed at 1440/390, which explains several layout bugs that one look would have caught.

Cross-app: the four apps clearly read as one family (palette 0.958, type 1.0 in the gates match what is visible). The differences that matter are the inconsistent bloom clip edges, inconsistent serif usage, the blog-only brand icon, and the inconsistent media placeholders.
promptFixes: Bloom recipe (spec gap, highest priority): replace 'Inside the header or empty-state section (position: relative; overflow: hidden)' with: 'Put the bloom in a full-bleed band that spans the viewport width, not the container: a wrapper with position:relative; overflow-x:clip; overflow-y:visible around the header, and on the page root overflow-x:clip. The bloom must never be clipped by the container or by the header bottom. Either give the header min-height >= the visible bloom height (top offset + 560px), or add mask-image: radial-gradient(closest-side, #000 70%, transparent) to the SVG so any edge is feathered. Verification: no straight edge on the bloom anywhere; the bloom may only leave the screen through the viewport edge.'

Rule 6 serif word (spec gap): change to 'One serif italic word per page title, and never the whole title: one-word titles stay fully sans. Use the serif word only on titles of two or more words, and only where the per-app list allows it.' Add a Never-list line: 'A whole heading set in serif.' In the Settings bullet, replace 'optional' with 'no serif word on settings titles'.

Dark bloom (spec gap): add a second filter mn-wash-night without the grain composite and rim darkening (wash plus a softened rim at a lighter tint), and say: 'In dark use mn-wash-night; the bloom must read lighter than color.surface.default, never darker.' Show the dark variant in the recipe.

Mobile bloom (spec gap): replace the 360x288 / top -60 / right -140 geometry with 'Under breakpoint.md the bloom sits above the h1 band only: max 240x192, top -80px, right -120px, and its visible part must not overlap the lead paragraph; if it would, omit the bloom on mobile.' Add to Verification: 'At 390px nothing but the h1 overlaps the bloom.'

Text field height (agent mistake the spec already forbids, strengthen it): in Text field Anatomy add 'Set height explicitly (height: var(--size-control); box-sizing: border-box); never rely on line-height; inputs placed in flex rows with chips or buttons share the row's control height and align-items:center against size.control.' Add to Verification: 'Every input renders at 32, 36 or 40px; none is shorter than size.controlSm.'

Mobile navigation (agent mistake the spec already covers, move it into the rules): add to Layout adaptation 'Under breakpoint.md, any nav with more than 3 links (header or sidebar) collapses into the two-line menu button plus sheet; nav links never overflow the viewport.' Add to Verification: 'At 390px document scrollWidth equals the viewport width on every route.'

Mobile tables (spec gap): add to Table: 'Under breakpoint.md, wrap the table in an overflow-x:auto container with min-width:0 on its grid or flex parents so the page never scrolls horizontally; keep the first column at least 140px and do not let primary text wrap beyond 2 lines; trailing action columns (Revoke) stay reachable.' Alternatively specify a stacked-row pattern for tables with 5 or more columns.

Media placeholder (spec gap, the base apps have no photos): add a 'No asset' state to Media frame: 'color.surface.tray, the hatch pattern, one centered 20px outline image icon in color.text.tertiary; never a large or filled glyph.' Add to Never: 'Placeholder illustrations (mountains, suns) in media frames.'

Switch off state (spec gap, contrast): change the switch track to 'off: color.surface.subtle fill with 1px color.text.tertiary border (at least 3:1 against the card in both themes)'. Do the same for the checkbox resting border if it uses border.strong on raised.

Product and detail titles (spec gap): in the Typography table add 'Object detail h1 (product, project, record): h1Article 44 / heading / h1Article tracking; Page h1 56 is for index and overview pages only.' Add to Hierarchy guidance: 'Do not stack an h2 that repeats the h1 ('Projects' then 'All projects').'

Mono rule (spec gap, tighten it): change rule 7 to name 'all dates, amounts, IDs and counts in tables, spec rows and key/value rows', and state that spec rows are '180px mono key + value'. Point the commerce Details list at the spec-row pattern explicitly in the Store bullet.
Sticky action bar (spec gap): add 'Pages with the sticky bar add bottom padding equal to the bar height plus space.16 so no content ends under it.'

Equal-height cards (spec gap): add to Card: 'In a row of cards with different content, align to the top (align-items:start) unless the cards are the same kind; a chart card never stretches to an adjacent list's height.'

Harness/verification (process): neither agent could build or view the apps, so the spec's 'checked at 1440 and 390' step was never done. Either let the generate step run the dev server plus a screenshot pass, or turn the visual checks into self-checkable code rules (explicit control heights, overflow-x:clip on root, min-width:0 on flex children) as above. Also capture focus, hover, error and empty states in the screenshot set so componentStates can actually be judged.
